newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Wind, lack of equipment, blamed in Mongolia crash.
newsitem.headline: Wind, lack of equipment, blamed in Mongolia crash.

text.p: Mongolian investigators on Thursday said lack of equipment at the Mandelgobi airport combined with wind shear caused the crash of small passenger plane earlier this month in which eight people died.
The Chinese-built Yun-12 plane crashed to the ground from a height of about 30 metres (110 ft) on June 10 as it was coming in to land when it was hit by wind shear, investigators told Reuters.
They said the Mandelgobi airport in the southern Gobi had no equipment to measure the direction and speed of wind up to an altitude of 1,000 metres (yards).
Human error and mechanical failure were not involved, they added.
Four of the 12 people on board survived the crash, including the two crew.
